result.topic_en: Case analysis of a system of partial differential equations (numbered 11, 12, 13, 22, 23, 33) in variables alpha, beta for functions a, c, m, reducing to the ODE f'' + k^2 f'/f^3 = 0, followed by integration of a resulting quadratic differential form (line element) in new coordinates.
result.transcription:
Aus (12) folgt $\frac{\partial \frac{a}{c}}{\partial\beta} = 0$, man kann folglich $\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta} = 0$ machen.
Dann folgt aus (11) $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} = m\,\varphi(\alpha)$ aus (22) $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha} = m\,\psi(\beta)$
[-folglich $\frac{\partial c}{\varphi(\alpha)\partial\beta} = \frac{\partial c}{\psi(\beta)\partial\alpha}$-] $\psi(\beta)\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} - \varphi(\alpha)\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha} = 0$
[-man kann also $c = f(\alpha+\beta)$ machen-]
[-dann wird $\frac{f(\alpha+\beta)}{\dots} = \varphi(\alpha) = \psi(\beta) = \text{const} = \frac{1}{k}$-]
also kann man entweder $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha} = m$ $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} = m$ [-$\dots = 0$-] machen

$c = f(\alpha+\beta)$
$m = f'(\alpha+\beta)$
dann folgt aus (13)
[-$f''$-] $ac = f^2\varphi(\alpha) + \psi(\alpha)$
man kann also $ac = \psi(\alpha)$ machen
dann folgt aus (12) $[-k-]\,c\frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta} + [-f^2-]\left(\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}\right)^2 = 0$ oder $f'' + \frac{(\psi(\alpha))^2}{f^3}f' = 0$, $\frac{f^3 f''}{f'} = -\psi(\alpha)^2 = \text{const} = -k^2$
$f'' + \frac{k^2}{f^3}f' = 0$ also $ac = \text{const} = k$
$a = \frac{k}{f}$ $c = f$. $m = f'$
[-Aus Vergleichung dieser Werthe giebt (23)-] | In Folge von $ac = \text{const}$. giebt (23) $\frac{\partial m}{\partial\alpha} - a\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta} = 0$, oder $f'' + \frac{k^2}{f^3}f' = 0$
und (33) $\frac{\partial^2 a^2}{\partial\beta^2} - 2\frac{\partial^2 m}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta} = 0$ | In Folge von $ac = \text{const}$ und $\frac{\partial m}{\partial\alpha} - a\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta} = 0$ werden (23) und (33) erfüllt.

[-wenn $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha} = 0$ $c = f(\beta)$ $m = f'(\beta)$
folgt aus (13) $ac = f^2\varphi(\alpha) + \psi(\alpha)$ aus (12) $a = 0$ oder $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} = 0$ $c = \text{const}$. $a = \psi(\alpha)$ und folglich $a = 0$ gemacht werden kann.
(23) ...
wenn $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} = 0$ $c = f(\alpha)$ $m = f'(\alpha)$
aus (12) $\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta} = 0$-]
Wenn $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}$ oder $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} = 0$, $m = \text{const}$. Wenn $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha} = 0$. folgt aus (13) $ac = c^2\varphi(\alpha) + \psi(\alpha)$ man kann also $ac = \psi(\alpha)$ machen
und aus (12) $\frac{a}{c} = \varphi(\alpha)$; man kann also
und ... $\frac{a}{c} = \varphi(\alpha)$ man kann also $a = 0$ machen.
wenn $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} = 0$ folgt aus (12) $\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta} = 0$, man kann also $a = 0$ machen.

[Rand rechts:] Aus $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}$ oder $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta} = 0$ folgt $m = \varphi(\alpha)\psi(\beta)$
und wegen (12) $\frac{a}{c} = \chi(\alpha)$ man kann also $a = 0$ machen.

[-$f' = \frac{k^2}{2f^2} \dots$-] $\alpha = x + yi$ $\beta = x - yi$
$(f\,dy + \frac{k}{f}dy_1)^2 + 2f'(dx^2 + dy^2)$
[-$f^2dy^2 + 2k\,dy\,dy_1 + 2f'dx^2 + \text{const}\,dy^2$-]
$2f' = k_1^2 - \frac{k^2}{f^2}$ $f^2dy^2 + 2k\,dy_1dy + 2f'dx^2 + k_1^2dy^2$
$2f'dx^2 = 2\frac{df^2}{f'} = \frac{4f^2df^2}{f^2k_1^2 - k^2} = d\zeta^2$
$d\zeta = \frac{2f\,df}{\sqrt{f^2k_1^2 - k^2}}$ $\zeta = \frac{2}{k_1^2}\sqrt{f^2k_1^2 - k^2}$
$\frac{k_1^4}{4}\zeta^2 = f^2k_1^2 - k^2$
$f^2 = \frac{k^2}{k_1^2} + \frac{k_1^2}{4}\zeta^2$
$d\zeta^2 + (k_1dy + \frac{k}{k_1}dy_1)^2 + \frac{k_1^2}{4}\zeta^2dy^2$
[-$dr^2$-] $\zeta = r$. $\frac{k_1}{2}y = \varrho$
$k_1y + \frac{k}{k_1}y_1 = z$
$r = \text{const}$. $z - \frac{2k}{k_1^2}\varrho = \text{const}$.
